The Kaneki harness before and after the fix

How the feature-flags ticket actually ran, session by session with exact transcript references; what each part of the harness does today and after the fix; and the work plan to get there.

  • Updated2026-11-27
  • Harnesskaneki-harness @ d14a71d

  • StatusProposal for your review

The harness after the fix, in one screen

In short

After the fix the harness decides test and evidence validity itself, using driver checks plus a cited agent judge. It runs evidence through harness-owned tools instead of throwaway scripts, writes test cases before coding, and measures its own cost correctly. You are asked only about business, infra or critical logic that has no citation to decide on. The tester notebook is a read-only view for looking back.

  1. Review nodes become trusted judges, not a gate for you. Each question is determinable (decided by driver code), judgeable (decided by an independent agent that must cite the requirement and the evidence), or escalated to you (business, infra, or critical logic without a basis). S1
  2. Evidence needs no throwaway scripts. Live cases become repo tests written in coding, or declarative steps run by sdlc evidence run, against an environment started by sdlc env up. In feature-flags the agent wrote 12 script files (~1,000 lines), patched them 37 times and lost 2 runs to the environment. S2S3
  3. Fewer generations. Test cases are written right after the plan and feed coding. Mutation checks prove test strength. Reviews run in parallel. Small fixes take a small path. The loop cap is enforced.
  4. Cost is measured, not guessed. The ticket recorded 2,284,355 tokens; the logs show 113,735,785. Two driver bugs and two unrecorded runs explain the gap. S4S5
  5. Failures stop early. The CLI is reachable from units, sdlc check runs before every hand-back, prepare leaves a ready-to-build baseline, and the ship path is checked at onboarding.

≈ 3 htarget, same size (after)

The whole lifecycle, before and after

Before: 13 nodes in a strict sequence, test cases after code review, and you as the judge of last resort. After: a shorter lane with independent work in parallel, judges with authority, and you only for escalations.

Mechanism by mechanism, before and after

The same comparison by concern rather than by node, so each part of the harness can be reviewed on its own.

Cost measurement

Before

Three different totals (997,808 · 2,284,355 · 51,561,957). --tokens is the last context size. Controllers count 0. Abandoned runs are not recorded. S11S4S12

After

One total from the logs: units, controller, side calls, split into fresh, cache write, cache read and output, plus USD. Every dispatch is recorded, including abandoned ones.

CLI and gates

Before

66 failed CLI calls in units; about 10 G7 refusals after hand-back for sections, verdict lines, short citations and schemas.

After

Absolute launcher path in every packet; digest <path>; sdlc check = the gate as a dry run, required before hand-back; bare unique filenames accepted.

Environment

Before

No deps at coding; local Postgres max_connections=20 exhausted by the Neon proxy; the agent wrote its own connection reaper; the profile baseUrl pointed at production. S9

After

sdlc env up|down owns DB sizing or pooling, migrations, the seeded test account (.sdlc/test-env), the app server and health checks. Onboarding verifies the evidence target.

Review authority

Before

Reviewers report; doubts become questions to you. 2 of the 4 waits over 10 minutes (45 of 120 minutes) were questions a judge could have settled.

After

Driver decides what is determinable; the judge decides what is judgeable, with citations; you get only escalations (section 6). S1

Evidence execution

Before

12 script files (~1,000 lines) written per ticket; 21 writes and 16 in-place patches across 20 runs; phaseB run 7 times. S2S3

After

Live cases are repo e2e specs from coding, or declarative steps run by a tested harness runner; smoke-first, resumable, failure-classified (section 7).

Test cases and evidence data

Before

Markdown tables; one status per case; "NOT EXECUTED" covers both "never ran" and "ran but partly asserted"; evidence = a test name. S14S17

After

testcases.json (checks per case, acceptance criteria, risk) and evidence.json (observed value and source per check), written by tests via evidence(); documents are rendered from them.

Scheduling and loops

Before

One node at a time S15; loopCap: 2 set but coding reached generation 5 S18; small doc/test fixes restarted 4 nodes.

After

Every ready node runs; the loop cap counts manual invalidations; tests-only and docs-only fixes take change → check.

Controller

Before

One Opus session ran 5 h 20 m and 212 API calls; context grew from 60 K to 333 K and ran out; controllers were 55% of tokens. S3

After

Fresh session per phase from HANDOFF.md; hand-backs of at most 15 lines; no whole-artifact reads; optional Sonnet controller.

Ship

Before

CM016 trailer added by the controller; stray files after the receipt; my-git not installed; guard reads $R literally; GH008 PR sections missing (38462dbc:436–909). S7

After

Ship backend checked at onboarding; closed nodes are immutable for the controller; untracked files cleaned before the receipt; drafts checked against repo rules.

Tester notebook

Before

To look back you read testcases.md (555 lines) and run-report.md (367 lines), then opened each test and log yourself.

After

A read-only page per ticket: criteria, findings with the class that settles each one, case cards with code, log and observed values, and change coverage. S19

How the review judges decide

The test-case judge and the evidence judge settle everything that has a basis in the ticket's requirements and the evidence. They escalate only what does not. S1

ClassWho decidesExamplesHow
DeterminableDriver codeSchema valid; every criterion has a critical case; observed = expected; test ran (ok line); test tagged with its check; every changed file coveredDeterministic rules EVD-A…E; the judge cannot overrule them
JudgeableJudge agentIs the expected value what the requirement says? Does the case test the requirement or a weaker proxy? Is the assertion strong enough? Is a partial check acceptable?Verdict valid only with a requirement citation + an evidence citation, both resolved and quoted verbatim
EscalateYouBusiness: requirement silent, ambiguous or conflicting, with no answer in questions.md. Infra: a surface cannot be provided. Critical logic: judges disagree, or confidence below High.One batch plus a push notification

What makes a judge trustworthy

  1. J1 · Independence

    The judge never wrote what it judges. Fresh read-only deep-tier unit.

  2. J2 · Machine facts first

    The judge receives the driver's facts and fills only the judgement slots. A check the driver marks unobserved cannot be PASS.

  3. J3 · Mutation proof of test strength

    For critical checks the driver removes or flips the guarded line (for example the isFeatureEnabled gate) and requires the tagged test to fail. That settles "is this test vacuous?" without opinion, the class of gap behind coding generations 4 and 5.

  4. J4 · Two judges on critical items

    Two independent judges must agree; disagreement is by definition a critical-logic escalation.

  5. J5 · Calibration

    Verdicts go to evidence-judgement.json. When a later stage overturns one, reflect records a judge miss; a rising miss rate tightens escalation.

Running evidence without throwaway scripts

Root causeIn one sentence: the evidence node wrote new software for every ticket against an environment it also had to manage. 20 of the 30 run failures were environment problems (12 too many clients, 8 Neon Control plane request failed), 9 were brittle UI steps (6 selector, 3 timeout), and 1 was a failed login. S3S2
  1. E1 · Live cases are repo tests written in coding

    Coding writes them from testcases.json as e2e specs (Playwright test or supertest), next to the unit tests. They are code-reviewed, kept as regression tests, and run in CI. The evidence node runs them; it does not author them.

  2. E2 · Declarative steps for the rest

    Cases that do not belong in the repo become data that a tested runner executes. Steps are validated against a schema before the run, so there are no syntax errors and no patching in place.

    { "case": "TC-61", "params": ["P1", "…", "P11"], "as": "userA", "setup": [{ "flag": { "lms": false } }],
  "steps":  [{ "page": "goto", "url": "${P}" }],
  "expect": [{ "check": "a1", "status": 404 }, { "check": "a2", "textAbsent": ["${subject.title}"] }] }
  3. E3 · sdlc env up | down

    The harness owns the database (sized or pooled per the profile), migrations, the seeded test account, the app server and health checks, reused across cases and tickets. Agents never start servers or touch DB connections.

  4. E4 · Runner rules

    Smoke run first (one case per surface), then the batch; each case isolated; resume from the last case; wait on network and DOM events, never sleep; per-unit time and token cap.

  5. E5 · A project evidence kit that grows

    Helpers such as "toggle lms" or "soft-navigate in subject" live in .sdlc/adapters/evidence/<project> and are tested once. When a step is missing, reflect proposes adding it.

Failure handling by class

ClassExample in feature-flagsRunner behaviour
Infratoo many clients, Neon 500sRetry with backoff at most 2 times, then stop and escalate as infra
Step errorSelector not found, timeoutsReport with a DOM snapshot; the agent fixes the step data once; a second failure is escalated
Product failureObserved ≠ expectedA real FAIL, recorded once, never retried
